title: Email breach checker
description: Check where an email address appears in available breach sources.
overview: JoeScan combines available email exposure sources and removes duplicate breach entries when they can be matched. Reports help you understand which incidents may affect an address.
steps: Review breach names and available dates.
Inspect the exposed data categories supplied by the source.
Use the report to prioritize password changes and account checks.
limits: Coverage varies by provider. A result with no matches does not prove an address has never leaked. Provider outages and incomplete data are not clean results.
data: Your email is sent to the configured lookup services. Saved scan reports belong to your signed-in account.

title: Password strength & exposure check
description: Understand password strength and check for known exposure.
overview: JoeScan combines a password-strength assessment with a known-exposure check and a cryptographically secure password generator.
steps: Assess length and predictable patterns.
Check known exposure using a hash-prefix lookup.
Generate a new password and store it in your password manager.
limits: Strength estimates cannot predict every attack. A password absent from the available exposure dataset may still be compromised. Avoid reusing passwords.
data: The raw password is not stored in scan history or sent in plaintext for the exposure lookup. A hash prefix is sent for that lookup; the match is checked locally.

title: Suspicious link checker
description: Review warning signs before opening an unfamiliar link.
overview: JoeScan examines a URL for suspicious characteristics and provides an initial assessment to support safer browsing.
steps: Review the domain and URL structure.
Inspect the reported warning signs and available reputation context.
Use the suggested next steps before entering credentials or payment data.
limits: This is not a sandbox or a guarantee that a page is safe. A site can change after a check. Do not open a suspicious link just because no warning appeared.
data: Remove private access tokens and personal details from URLs before submitting them. Analysis may involve an external provider.

title: Phishing message analysis
description: Spot suspicious language and requests in messages.
overview: JoeScan reviews submitted message text for indicators of scams, phishing and social engineering, then explains practical precautions.
steps: Paste a message with unnecessary personal information removed.
Review suspicious requests, urgency and impersonation cues.
Verify the sender through a separate trusted channel.
limits: AI analysis can miss scams or flag legitimate messages. It does not authenticate the sender, inspect your mailbox or guarantee attachment safety.
data: Message text is sent to the configured analysis provider. Remove one-time codes, passwords and confidential content before submitting.

title: Domain & DNS lookup
description: Review domain registration and DNS information.
overview: JoeScan brings available registration and DNS details together to help you understand a domain before relying on it.
steps: Review available registration details.
Inspect DNS records and hosting context.
Use the findings alongside your own checks of the organization.
limits: Registration details may be redacted, unavailable or outdated. A recent domain is not automatically malicious, and an old domain is not automatically trustworthy.
data: Domain queries may be sent to public lookup services. Do not include credentials or private tokens in your input.

title: Social profile research
description: Organize public social-profile leads for careful review.
overview: JoeScan supports public-profile research with search candidates and AI-assisted summaries. It helps you decide where to investigate further.
steps: Search a public identifier you are authorized to research.
Follow source links and compare the available context.
Treat uncertain associations as unconfirmed.
limits: Similar names and usernames can produce false matches. AI summaries are not independent evidence of identity, ownership or wrongdoing.
data: Research only publicly available information for legitimate purposes. Do not submit private conversations or credentials.

title: Exposure watchlist
description: Keep selected targets together for follow-up checks.
overview: JoeScan provides an account-based watchlist for tracking selected targets and reviewing available follow-up findings.
steps: Add an authorized target to your watchlist.
Review monitoring status and available updates.
Investigate changes and remove targets you no longer need.
limits: Monitoring depends on source coverage, service availability and your plan. It is not continuous visibility into every leak or a guarantee of immediate notification.
data: Watchlist targets are stored in your account to support follow-up checks. Account deletion includes the monitoring state.

title: Threat intelligence map
overview: JoeScan visualizes available threat intelligence to help you understand reported network activity in context.
steps: Explore the supplied feed and geographic context.
Review source details and timestamps where available.
Use the map as background context for further investigation.
limits: A marker is not proof of an ongoing attack against you. Feed coverage, location estimates and refresh times vary. The map is not a live view of all global attacks.
data: The map provides general intelligence. Do not interpret its public indicators as private information about individual people.

title: 3D threat visualization
description: Explore threat information in an interactive globe.
overview: JoeScan offers a three-dimensional view of available threat information for visual exploration.
steps: Navigate the globe and inspect available markers.
Compare source context with the map view.
Investigate a reported indicator separately when necessary.
limits: Visualization does not create additional evidence. Geographic markers may be approximate and feed information can be incomplete. Access depends on your plan.
data: This view presents general threat information and does not publish your personal scan history.

title: Team workspace
description: Coordinate eligible account workflows with a team.
overview: JoeScan provides team-related account tools for eligible plans, alongside the security checks available in the workspace.
steps: Review your current plan and team settings.
Invite only intended collaborators.
Periodically review and remove unnecessary access.
limits: Team access does not remove the need for individual authorization or security review. Availability depends on the current plan and configuration.
data: Invitations contain the information needed to manage collaboration. Do not place passwords or confidential scan details in invitation fields.
